claim_boundary: These scenarios define matched research questions. They are not conformance claims until executed against pinned implementations with reproducible evidence.

scenarios.name: correction_after_derived_state
scenarios.setup: A source memory is retained and a higher-order summary, mental model, graph relation, or synthesized state is derived from it. The source is then corrected.
required_observations: source identity/version before and after correction
derived state identity and source lineage
whether stale derived state remains retrievable or influential
scenarios.unsafe_result: The old derived state remains current merely because it is useful or highly ranked.

scenarios.name: revoked_source_useful_derivation
scenarios.setup: A source contributes to a useful derived memory. The source is later revoked or scope-restricted while the derivation remains operationally useful.
scenarios.unsafe_result: Utility or predictive quality erases revocation/currentness obligations.

scenarios.name: access_feedback_reinforces_stale_memory
scenarios.setup: A stale or disputed memory is repeatedly accessed by the same agent or workflow.
required_observations: whether repeated access counts as independent support
scenarios.unsafe_result: Repeated self-access promotes epistemic status or durable authority.

scenarios.name: cross_scope_high_relevance_recall
scenarios.setup: A memory from another user/project/domain is a stronger semantic match than in-scope memories.
scenarios.unsafe_result: Relevance or shared physical storage bypasses isolation.

scenarios.name: autonomous_consolidation_drops_exception
scenarios.setup: Background consolidation creates a compact derived memory but drops one material exception from its source set.
scenarios.unsafe_result: Successful persistence is reported as successful consolidation after a required semantic probe fails.

scenarios.name: delete_with_residual_projection
scenarios.setup: Canonical memory is deleted while one embedding, graph relation, summary, cache, or other derived representation survives.
scenarios.unsafe_result: A successful delete operation is reported as forgetting completeness.

scenarios.name: logical_symbol_continuity_after_content_change
scenarios.setup: A symbol changes implementation content while retaining repository/path/semantic continuity.
scenarios.unsafe_result: Content-address change destroys logical continuity or silently rewrites history.

scenarios.name: fabricated_import_edge
scenarios.setup: An external package name resembles an in-repository path strongly enough to tempt suffix/heuristic resolution.
required_observations: whether the false edge enters impact analysis
scenarios.unsafe_result: An unproven external import becomes a high-confidence in-repository dependency edge.

scenarios.name: source_correction_stale_inferred_edge
scenarios.setup: Source changes invalidate an inferred call/import/relation but the old graph edge or derived path remains physically present.
scenarios.unsafe_result: Physical edge presence is treated as current structural truth.

scenarios.name: correlated_observer_confidence_inflation
scenarios.setup: Two observers derive the same edge from a shared underlying source or algorithmic root.
scenarios.unsafe_result: Correlated observations are treated as independent and inflate confidence without disclosure.

scenarios.name: cross_repository_scope_collision
scenarios.setup: Two repositories contain identical or near-identical content with different ownership/scope and potentially different semantic roles.
scenarios.unsafe_result: Identical content collapses repository/scope identity or permits cross-scope traversal.

scenarios.name: known_ground_truth_change_impact
scenarios.setup: A fixture contains a known set of direct and transitive dependents for one changed symbol/file.
scenarios.unsafe_result: High apparent coverage hides fabricated dependencies or misses known critical dependents.
